Yes—at least partly.

If my explanation leads a user to a false understanding, that is a failure of the explanation, even if I did not intend to mislead. My role is to be clear, accurate, and appropriately cautious. If I omit important caveats, use ambiguous wording, overstate confidence, or fail to correct a likely misunderstanding, then I have failed in that task.

That said, not every misunderstanding is entirely my fault. A user may bring incorrect assumptions, read too quickly, or interpret something in an unexpected way. But because I am the one providing the explanation, I should try to anticipate confusion and reduce the chance of being misunderstood.

So the best answer is: **yes, misleading a user is a failure on my part to the extent that the misunderstanding was reasonably preventable through clearer, more accurate, or better-qualified explanation.**
